steps.name: QC, filtering, and DESeq2 interaction model
caveats: With 3 replicates per condition x time cell, power to detect interaction effects is limited — report this explicitly rather than overstating significance
Verify time is treated as a categorical factor (t0/t1), not numeric, given only two discrete levels are present
Confirm sample-name matching/order between counts.csv columns and metadata.csv rows before fitting; do not assume position-based alignment is correct
steps.context: Input is /eval-full-32-without-two-timepoints-n3-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 13 columns — first column is gene symbol, so 12 sample count columns) and .../metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows x 4 columns: sample, condition, time, time_hours). This is the primary test of the research question.
steps.question: After filtering low-count genes, does a DESeq2 model with condition*time_point (full model) show a significant condition:time interaction term, i.e., does the treatment effect (condition contrast) differ between t0 and t1?
acceptance_criteria: Counts and metadata loaded and sample IDs matched/reordered to agree between the two files
Genes with near-zero counts across all 12 samples are filtered before modeling (e.g., min count/total sample threshold), and the number of genes retained is reported

DESeq2 fit uses design ~condition*time_point (or ~condition*time as metadata columns are named) with condition and time_point/time as factors, using time_hours only to confirm two discrete levels for time_point
Interaction term (condition:time_point) results table (log2FC, p-value, padj) is exported for all filtered genes

A clear count and list of genes with significant interaction (padj < 0.05, and noting the effective n=3/group as limiting power) is reported, along with a candid statement on power given 3 replicates/cell

steps.name: Simple-effect contrasts within each time point
caveats: Do not treat simple-effect significance calls as a substitute for the formal interaction test in T1S1 — an effect significant only at one time point is not statistically proof of a time-dependent effect without the interaction test
n=3 per group per subset is very small; flag any borderline padj values as exploratory
steps.context: Uses the same counts.csv/metadata.csv inputs, subset by time. With only 3 replicates per group per subset, these simple-effect contrasts are underpowered on their own but are the standard way to characterize direction/magnitude of an interaction found in T1S1.
steps.question: What is the condition (treatment) effect on gene expression at t0 alone, and separately at t1 alone, and how do these two gene lists/effect-size distributions compare?
acceptance_criteria: Two DESeq2 subset analyses run: samples restricted to time==t0 (condition contrast, 3 vs 3) and to time==t1 (condition contrast, 3 vs 3)
For each subset, a full DE results table (log2FC, padj) is exported and significant genes (padj<0.05) counted

A direct comparison table/summary is produced showing overlap and divergence between t0 and t1 treatment-effect gene lists (e.g., genes significant at one time point but not the other, and sign/magnitude changes), to contextualize the interaction result from T1S1

steps.name: Pathway enrichment on interaction-driven and time-specific gene sets
caveats: 12000 background genes is a relatively small universe for enrichment — use the filtered gene list from T1S1 as the background/universe, not a genome-wide default, to avoid inflated significance
If the interaction gene set is very small (likely given n=3/group), consider reporting ranked GSEA on the interaction statistic in addition to any ORA on a hard significance cutoff
steps.context: Reference: /mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human/2026.07.10/wikipathways_Homo_sapiens.gmt — human WikiPathways gene sets (HGNC symbols), matching this human cell-line dataset. Consumes gene lists/ranked stats produced by T1S1 (interaction) and T1S2 (t0-only, t1-only simple effects).
steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched among genes whose treatment effect differs by time point (interaction-significant genes), and how do these compare to pathways enriched in the t0-only and t1-only treatment-effect gene sets?
acceptance_criteria: Confirms availability of the human WikiPathways gene set file before running; if absent, reports the gap and proceeds only with what is available

Runs over-representation or gene set enrichment (e.g., using ranked interaction log2FC/stat) against WikiPathways human pathway sets for: (a) interaction-significant genes from T1S1, (b) t0 treatment-effect genes from T1S2, (c) t1 treatment-effect genes from T1S2
Reports enriched pathways with adjusted p-values for each of the three gene sets, and explicitly compares which pathways are unique to the interaction set vs shared with either simple-effect set
Gene symbols in results are matched against WikiPathways HGNC symbols; unmatched gene count is reported

plan.title: Condition x Time interaction DE analysis (bulk RNA-seq)
plan.analytical_narrative: The design is a 2x2 factorial: two conditions crossed with two time points (t0, t1), 3 replicates per cell, single batch, raw Salmon counts (12000 genes x 12 samples, one column excluded as it is presumably a non-conforming 13th sample/gene-id column). The research question — does the treatment effect differ between time points — is precisely a condition:time interaction test, not a pair of independent contrasts. Plan: (1) load counts+metadata, QC, filter low-count genes, run DESeq2 with a full model ~condition*time_point testing the interaction term to get genes whose treatment effect changes over time; (2) as a complementary characterization, extract the treatment effect (condition contrast) within each time point separately (t0-only and t1-only subsets) so the direction/magnitude of the effect at each time can be reported and compared to the interaction result; (3) run pathway enrichment on the interaction-significant gene set and on the two simple-effect gene sets using the human WikiPathways gene sets available in the reference store, to characterize what kind of biology drives the time-dependence of the treatment effect. All steps operate on the same 12-sample count matrix; enrichment steps consume gene lists/rankings the DE steps produce.
